notes.title: Proposal: give the Saltmarsh League room

thread.text: The Saltmarsh League holds one province, Venetia, with 25 settlements packed into it (8 towns, 4 castles, 13 villages) inside the Azure Crown. In play that is one small fief-sized patch for a whole realm: its lords would have nowhere to march and one siege could end it. Proposal: (1) the League takes the two Azure coast provinces beside it, Lorraine and Peyrolles (both Bayfolk country already, 12 settlements); (2) Venetia splits in two, a northern lagoon around Brinemere, Chalmont and Fresnay and a southern one around Saltmere, Chioggia Vel and Hondeval; (3) the crowded centre thins to about 3 towns, 2 castles and 8 villages, the rest moving out into the new provinces. The League ends with 4 provinces and about 30 settlements; the Azure Crown keeps 10 provinces. Agree, change, or turn it down here; nothing on the map moves until you say.

The owner agreed this in conversation (2026-11-17). Built: Lorraine and Peyrolles pass to the League with their settlements (their people stay Bayfolk); Venetia's centre moves to the southern lagoon and a new province, Mestre, holds the northern one; Brinemere, Saltmere, Hondeval, Chioggia Vel, Fresnay, Taillefer and the outer villages stay (Mestre 6, Venetia 8); eleven settlements moved out into Lorraine (12 now) and Peyrolles (11). The League holds 4 provinces and 37 settlements; the Azure Crown 10 provinces.

HOLDS (docs/archive/HOLDS.md HD4) for the Azure Crown: towns become rare (2-3 a realm), castles common. KEEP AS TOWNS: Peyrolles, Dammartin, Coralto (the capital first, then the best ports and road hubs, spread apart). BECOME CASTLES: Polderwick, Valcourt, Brinehold, Elgfoss, Glenmorrow, Lancrois. NEW HOLDS: Montrevel in Normandy at (-184.3, -45.2); Castelroc in Castile at (-284.4, -176.5); Haut-Brisac in Valen at (-478.8, -46.0) (each on a road or its province's middle, where a province has no seat or one seat on a frontier, at least 25 units from any seat; names in the realm's style). Villages bind to their nearest seat by themselves. Agree, or tell me what to change (a town to keep, a hold to move or rename). Nothing changes until you say so.
The owner asked me to decide (2026-11-19): applied as proposed. Castles now carry a rank for HD5: 3 great castle (former towns that were ports or road hubs), 2 castle, 1 tower house (the new holds).
Moved Montrevel, Castelroc, Haut-Brisac to stand at least 18 units from any village (the drawn castles stand a median 28 from theirs); same province.

Draft: the Chapter of Tarn's four highland provinces as one plateau, about 22 units above the plain, with cliffs along its west and south rims. The only ways up are where the roads cross the cliffs; those gaps are the passes, so the order's land is a fortress you enter by a few roads. Keep, move or drop it?

Draft: the northern highlands (Bergen, Viborg, Skane) as a high bare plateau, the fjell, 26 units up. The west coast from Novgorod to Oslo falls to the sea in cliffs: no landings there, only the ports. Keep, move or drop it?

Draft: the badlands (Mosul, Tabriz, Aleppo, Basra, Damascus) as a raised mesa country, 16 units up. An escarpment faces west over the coast at Alexandria and Shiraz, and the south coast below Damascus and Medina is sea cliff. Armies from the coast climb to it by the roads. Keep, move or drop it?

notes.title: Relief: the Vespran hills and the Dalmatian gorge

thread.text: Draft: Vespra's hill country (Macedon, Thessaly, Verona, Dalmatia, Thrace, Apulia) as rolling uplands, 10 units up, and the river through Dalmatia cut into a gorge between cliffs from the ridge down to the plain. The gorge is crossed only at its bridges. Keep, move or drop it?
Draft: the Khaganate's north-east (Krakow, Donets, Smolensk, the ridge) as hills, 9 units up; the rest of the steppe stays flat and open, the land for horse. Keep, move or drop it?
Draft: low downs round Brevon's ridge (Castile, Gascony, Roquebel), 7 units up. Brevon stays mostly lowland farm and forest, the contrast to the north and south. Keep, move or drop it?

notes.title: Relief: the 4x draft and what it changes

thread.text: This is the 4x draft (Data/world6.json, open it with tools/world.py --file Data/world6.json): every place, road and river of revision 17 at four times the distance, so towns stand about 650 units apart instead of 160 and the land between holds 16 times the room. Settlement count is unchanged, so density per area falls to a sixteenth. New here: uplands (plateau, massif, hills; a height each) and cliffs (the high side is on the left as the line runs; the teeth point down; roads crossing them are the passes). Next: fill the new room (more provinces in the wide gaps, wild land, waypoints). Which of the relief notes should stay?
